headline: Proves the subcritical Hénon–Lane–Emden conjecture: for small enough powers, these equations have no positive solution.
scope: Positive solutions on all of ℝⁿ, n ≥ 2, of −Δu = |x|^A v^p and −Δv = |x|^B u^q. Here p, q > 0 and A, B are real. Solutions need only be continuous at the origin.
plain: Some physics problems lead to two linked equations, where each unknown is driven by a power of the other. The Lane–Emden conjecture says that when the powers are small enough, no positive solution fills all of space. A weighted form adds powers of the distance from the origin. The paper settles both forms, with no extra assumption on symmetry or behaviour far away. A Lean statement covers the main theorem.
doesNot: This does not cover the critical case, where the inequality becomes an equality; there solutions can exist. It does not construct any solutions itself.
origin: This result comes from an unreleased OpenAI model, published in the openai/math release on 6 October 2026.

scorecard.significanceWhy: It settles the Lane–Emden conjecture for systems and its weighted form. Earlier proofs covered only low dimensions or added conditions.

explanation:
Start with one equation in three dimensions: −Δu = u⁵. Here Δ is the Laplacian, the sum of the second derivatives in each direction. It measures how much u at a point differs from its average nearby. The function u = (1 + r²/3)^(−1/2), where r is the distance from the origin, solves it. At r = 1, u = 0.866 and both sides equal 0.487. This solution is positive everywhere in space. Such a solution is called entire.

Now take two unknowns, u and v, with −Δu = v^p and −Δv = u^q. This is the Lane–Emden system. In dimension n the critical line is 1/(p+1) + 1/(q+1) = (n−2)/n. The example above sits exactly on it: n = 3 and p = q = 5 give 1/6 + 1/6 = 1/3. The conjecture says that strictly above this line, with smaller powers, no positive entire solution exists. For p = q = 4 in dimension 3, the left side is 0.4, which is above 1/3.

Gidas and Spruck proved the one-equation case[4]. Serrin and Zou proved the system in dimension 3 under a growth condition[5]. Later work removed that condition, and Souplet settled dimension 4[6]. The weighted Hénon form multiplies the right sides by |x|^A and |x|^B. Li and Zhang proved its dimension-3 case[7].

The paper claims the full answer in every dimension n ≥ 2[1]. When (n+A)/(p+1) + (n+B)/(q+1) > n − 2, no positive entire solution exists. Setting A = B = 0 gives the Lane–Emden conjecture[2]. No symmetry, boundedness or condition far from the origin is needed[3]. Together with a known radial existence theorem, it settles Phan's Conjecture C in full[8].

The weighted case is not a simple copy. Take dimension 5, with p = q = 4 and A = B = 3. The weighted test gives 8/5 + 8/5 = 3.2, above 3. The unweighted test gives 2/5, below 3/5[9]. The obstacle is that shifting the solution sideways no longer gives a solution, because the weights depend on the origin[10]. The paper instead zooms in and out about the origin. A local energy identity and a pressure estimate on short intervals then give a bound that forces a contradiction[11].

How sure is this? Lean, a computer proof checker, has a formal statement of the main nonexistence theorem. So the paper proves it, as far as the Lean statement matches the paper. The critical equality case is not in the Lean scope. No specialist review of the paper is published.
hypeCheck: A major result with a Lean statement of the main theorem. It covers only the strict inequality; the critical case is outside it. No specialist review is published.

glossary.meaning: The sum of the second derivatives of a function in each direction; it compares a value with its nearby average.
A solution defined on all of space, not just a bounded region.
The pair of equations −Δu = v^p and −Δv = u^q.
A factor |x|^A, a power of the distance from the origin, that multiplies a right-hand side.
The exact balance of powers, 1/(p+1) + 1/(q+1) = (n−2)/n, where solutions first appear.
Strictly on the side of the critical line with smaller powers.
A result saying that a solution on all of space must be trivial or cannot exist.

claims.text: For n ≥ 2, p, q > 0 and real A, B, the system has no strictly positive entire solution when (n+A)/(p+1) + (n+B)/(q+1) > n − 2.
claims.sourceLine: system has no strictly positive entire solution when
claims.sourceQuote: We prove the subcritical H\'enon--Lane--Emden conjecture: for every dimension $n\ge2$, positive powers $p,q$, and real weights $A,B$, the system has no strictly positive entire solution when $(n+A)/(p+1)+(n+B)/(q+1)>n-2$.

claims.text: Setting A = B = 0 gives the unweighted Lane–Emden conjecture as a corollary.
claims.sourceQuote: Theorem~\ref{thm:main} resolves Huang and Zou's Conjecture~B positively and yields Corollary~\ref{cor:lane-emden} by setting \(A=B=0\).
